claims.statement: SparkRoute bindings live only in ~/.config/sparkrun/proxy.yaml; there is no CLI add/remove command, and sparkrun proxy sync makes the running gateway match the file atomically.

The SparkRoute binding schema (fields: recipe, cluster/cluster_candidates, cold_start wait|reject, model, overrides, capabilities) is documented authoritatively by the installed plugin source at ~/.config/sparkrun/plugins/sparkroute/*/payload/, not upstream docs.
Bindings reference recipes in qualified @spark-forge/<recipe> form because plain names are ambiguous between the local checkout and the spark-forge registry.

All bindings use cold_start: wait so requests queue through multi-minute model swaps instead of erroring; idle-node-first placement is encoded via cluster_candidates order because SparkRoute 0.3.4 has no preempt-on-demand and eviction happens only via gateway idle timers on gateway-owned jobs.

The gateway admin API on port 4000 has no authentication and the proxy binds 0.0.0.0, offering GET/PUT /v1/config/managed-sets/operator, a validate endpoint, and CAS updates via expected_active_revision.

Strict validation rejects a sparkrun binding whose public model name an operator route owns; on 2026-11-03 three stale operator virtual models were removed via admin-API CAS replace with a backup at ~/.config/sparkrun/sparkroute/operator-set-backup-2026-11-03.json, keeping qwen38-27b and qwen38-27b:low as operator routes.

The proxy advertises model routes without live backends (5 routes exposed while both hosts were idle on 2026-11-03), autodiscovery sweeps dgx-pair every 30 s, and a discovered model name can collide with a reserved operator route of the same name.
proxy.env (mode 600) holds HF/NGC/NVIDIA/Ollama secrets and must never be printed into output or files.
The active gateway is the SparkRoute plugin 0.3.4 selected via the gateway.sparkroute feature, running on 0.0.0.0:4000, which the 2026-11-03 audit flags as a deliberate-or-not exposure decision.
